title: Swe senior scenario technical debt tradeoff
topic: Swe senior scenario technical debt tradeoff
question: Your team can ship a promised feature on time by hardcoding a workaround around a messy part of the system, or slip the deadline by a week to refactor that part properly first. How do you decide, and how do you communicate it?
idealAnswer:
Doesn't treat this as a purely technical call, weighs the actual cost of the workaround (who else depends on this module, how much harder does it get to fix later, what's the blast radius if it breaks) against the real cost of slipping a publicly committed date

Considers a middle path rather than treating it as strictly binary, e.g. shipping the workaround but scoping and scheduling the proper fix immediately after, with a concrete tracked ticket and timeline rather than a vague 'we'll fix it later'

Recognizes the specific risk of debt in a payments-adjacent module that other teams are starting to build on, technical debt compounds fastest exactly where more people are about to depend on it

Describes actually communicating the tradeoff to stakeholders in terms they can weigh, e.g. explaining the workaround's risk and cost in business terms, not just saying 'this is technically bad' and expecting that to be persuasive on its own

Shows ownership of the decision either way, a strong answer doesn't just describe the analysis, it commits to a call and explains why that call given the specific constraints
